[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/01/24 (Tue) 17:03  
[USER] User has a long haired rabbit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Long haired rabbits require regular grooming to prevent matting and tangling of their fur.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Daily brushing: Use a soft-bristled brush to gently brush your rabbit’s fur every day to remove any loose or tangled fur.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bathing: It is not recommended to bathe your rabbit too often as it can strip the natural oils from their fur. However, if your rabbit’s fur becomes excessively dirty or matted, a bath may be necessary. Use a gentle rabbit shampoo and make sure to rinse thoroughly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Trimming: Long haired rabbits may develop fur around their bottom that can become matted with feces. You should trim this fur regularly to prevent matting and keep your rabbit clean.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Check for mites: Long haired rabbits are more prone to getting mites, which can cause skin irritation and hair loss. Check your rabbit’s skin regularly for any signs of mites and treat if necessary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Diet: Feeding your rabbit a healthy diet with plenty of fiber can help prevent hairballs and promote healthy fur growth. Make sure they eat plenty of hay and fresh vegetables.  
[USER] User inquired about using regular human shampoo for their long haired rabbit if they run out of rabbit shampoo.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] No, it is not recommended to use regular human shampoo on your rabbit. Human shampoos are not formulated for a rabbit's skin and can be too harsh, causing dryness, irritation or even skin inflammation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It's important to use a shampoo specifically designed for rabbits, as they have a different pH level and their skin is much more sensitive than human skin.  
[USER] User asked if they can use scissors to trim their long haired rabbit's fur or if they need a specific type of trimmer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is not recommended to use scissors to trim your long haired rabbit's fur as it can be difficult to control, and you risk hurting your rabbit with the blades.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] You also risk accidentally cutting off more fur than intended and leaving patches that may take a long time to grow back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It's best to use specific rabbit trimmers with a guard to help prevent any accidental cuts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Scissors can also pull and cut fur unevenly, which can be very painful for your rabbit.
